name: Abu Dhabi
tagline: The UAE's stately capital — grand mosques, island museums, and a quieter cousin to Dubai.
description: Abu Dhabi is the UAE's cultural capital, home to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the Louvre Abu Dhabi, Yas Island theme parks, and a scenic waterfront corniche.
nearest_airport: Zayed International Airport — about 30 km from downtown

local_food.name: Al Machboos
local_food.description: Spiced rice with meat or fish, the Emirati take on biryani.

local_food.name: Shawarma
local_food.description: Spit-roasted meat wrapped in flatbread, a UAE street-food staple.

local_food.name: Luqaimat
local_food.description: Deep-fried dumplings drizzled with date syrup.

local_food.name: Balaleet
local_food.description: Sweet saffron vermicelli served with an omelette, a traditional Emirati breakfast.

experiences.name: Sunset at the Corniche
experiences.description: Walk or cycle the 8km waterfront promenade as the skyline lights up at dusk.

experiences.name: Desert safari
experiences.description: Dune-bash into the desert outside the city for camel rides and a Bedouin-style dinner.

experiences.name: Ferrari World ride
experiences.description: Experience Formula Rossa, one of the world's fastest roller coasters, on Yas Island.

experiences.name: Saadiyat museum walk
experiences.description: Spend a morning in the Louvre Abu Dhabi and Saadiyat's cultural district.

attractions.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
attractions.description: One of the world's largest mosques, with hand-knotted carpets and gleaming white marble domes.

attractions.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
attractions.description: A landmark museum under Jean Nouvel's perforated dome, showing art across cultures and eras.

attractions.name: Qasr Al Watan
attractions.description: The UAE's presidential palace, open to visitors for its ornate halls and a nightly light show.

attractions.name: Yas Island
attractions.description: Home to Ferrari World, Yas Waterworld and Yas Marina Circuit, the emirate's entertainment hub.

name: Bangalore
tagline: India's Garden City, where tech-park skylines meet leafy parks and a buzzing pub scene.
description: Bangalore (Bengaluru) is Karnataka's capital and India's tech capital — a green, high-altitude city of leafy boulevards, colonial-era gardens, and glass tech parks, famous for its year-round pleasant climate, craft breweries, and a food scene running from centuries.

local_food.name: Masala Dosa
local_food.description: A crisp rice-and-lentil crepe filled with spiced potato — try the original at Mavalli Tiffin Room (MTR) or Vidyarthi Bhavan.

local_food.name: Bisi Bele Bath
local_food.description: A hot, tangy rice dish cooked with lentils, vegetables and a distinctive spice blend, a Karnataka comfort-food staple.

local_food.name: Mysore Pak
local_food.description: A rich, ghee-soaked gram-flour sweet that originated in the Mysore royal kitchens and is sold across the city's sweet shops.

local_food.name: Filter Coffee
local_food.description: Strong South Indian coffee brewed in a traditional metal filter and served in a tumbler-and-dabarah set, a daily ritual at local darshinis.

experiences.name: Pub-hop in Indiranagar
experiences.description: Bangalore is India's craft-beer capital — spend an evening moving between microbreweries and rooftop bars in Indiranagar or Koramangala.

experiences.name: Cycle or walk through Cubbon Park
experiences.description: Join the car-free Sunday mornings in Cubbon Park for a relaxed walk, run or cycle through the city's green core.

experiences.name: Shop on Commercial Street
experiences.description: Browse the narrow lanes of one of Bangalore's oldest shopping districts for clothes, jewellery and street food.

experiences.name: Day trip to Nandi Hills
experiences.description: Head out before dawn to Nandi Hills, about 60 km away, for a sunrise over the Deccan plateau.

attractions.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
attractions.description: A 240-acre botanical garden laid out in the 18th century, home to a glasshouse modelled on London's Crystal Palace and a striking annual flower show.

attractions.name: Bangalore Palace
attractions.description: A Tudor-style royal palace built in 1887 for the Wadiyar family, with fortified towers, wood-carved interiors and manicured lawns.

attractions.name: Cubbon Park
attractions.description: A 300-acre green park in the heart of the city, ringed by colonial-era buildings including the High Court and State Central Library.

attractions.name: Vidhana Soudha
attractions.description: Karnataka's grand granite state legislature building, a Dravidian landmark especially striking when lit up on weekend evenings.

name: Cuttack
tagline: Odisha’s Silver City of rivers, heritage and legendary street food.
best_time_to_visit: October to March; November for Bali Jatra
description:
Cuttack is Odisha’s historic Silver City, set between the Mahanadi and Kathajodi rivers. Centuries of maritime trade, royal history and living craft traditions shape a city known for Barabati Fort, Cuttack Chandi Temple and delicate Tarakasi silver filigree.

Explore atmospheric old neighbourhoods and riverfronts, learn about Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Odisha’s maritime past, and follow the crowds to stalls serving the city’s signature Dahibara Aloodum. Visit during Durga Puja for elaborate pandals or during Bali Jatra for one of Odisha’s most celebrated fairs.
nearest_airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar — about 30 km

local_food.name: Dahibara Aloodum
local_food.description: Lentil dumplings soaked in yoghurt and topped with spicy potato curry, ghuguni and fresh garnishes.

local_food.name: Raghu Dahibara
local_food.description: A much-loved local take on Cuttack’s signature snack, typically enjoyed fresh from a street-side vendor.

local_food.name: Thunka Puri
local_food.description: A large, soft festive puri traditionally served with fragrant chhena tarkari during Bali Jatra.

local_food.name: Chhena Poda
local_food.description: Odisha’s caramelised baked cottage-cheese dessert, rich, smoky and widely available at local sweet shops.

local_food.name: Cuttack Mixture
local_food.description: A crunchy savoury blend of sev, lentils, nuts and spices that makes an easy snack or edible souvenir.

experiences.name: Taste Dahibara Aloodum
experiences.description: Follow local crowds to a street-food stall for Cuttack’s signature combination of soft dahi bara and spicy aloo dum.

experiences.name: Shop for silver filigree
experiences.description: Browse workshops and jewellery stores to see the delicate Tarakasi craft that gives Cuttack its Silver City nickname.

experiences.name: Walk the riverfront
experiences.description: Enjoy an early-morning or sunset walk along the Mahanadi and Kathajodi riverbanks for broad views and local life.

experiences.name: Experience Cuttack Durga Puja
experiences.description: If visiting in autumn, explore elaborate pandals and the city’s celebrated silver and gold festival backdrops.

attractions.name: Barabati Fort
attractions.description: Explore the ruins of a 14th-century riverside fort closely tied to Cuttack’s royal and military history.

attractions.name: Cuttack Chandi Temple
attractions.description: Visit the city’s revered presiding-deity temple, especially atmospheric during the annual Durga Puja season.

attractions.name: Netaji Birth Place Museum
attractions.description: See photographs, letters and personal objects at the restored ancestral home where Subhas Chandra Bose was born.

attractions.name: Odisha Maritime Museum
attractions.description: Discover Odisha’s river and maritime heritage inside a restored colonial-era workshop beside the Mahanadi.

attractions.name: Dhabaleswar Temple
attractions.description: Take a scenic trip to this Shiva temple on an island in the Mahanadi, reached by a pedestrian bridge.

name: Dhenkanal
tagline: A hill-ringed heritage town where a Shiva shrine crowns the peak and elephants roam the forest below.
description: Dhenkanal is an Odisha heritage town at the edge of the Eastern Ghats, home to the state's only fort-cum-palace, the hilltop Kapilash Shiva temple, and the Kapilash Wildlife Sanctuary — a key elephant corridor linking the region's forests.
nearest_airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar — about 75 km

local_food.name: Dhenkanal Bara
local_food.description: A famous urad-dal fritter from the town, crisp outside and soft within — considered one of Odisha's best.

local_food.name: Chhena Poda
local_food.description: A caramelised baked cottage-cheese dessert enjoyed across Odisha.

local_food.name: Dalma
local_food.description: A comforting lentil-and-vegetable stew, lightly tempered with cumin, garlic and red chilli.

local_food.name: Pakhala Bhata
local_food.description: Fermented rice soaked in water and curd, served with fried fish, potato and papad — a staple Odia lunch.

experiences.name: Climb Kapilash hill
experiences.description: Take the 1,352-step pilgrim stairway, or the hill road, up to the Shiva temple for panoramic views of the surrounding plains.

experiences.name: Spot elephants at Kapilash Sanctuary
experiences.description: Visit the elephant rescue centre and look out for wild elephants moving through this active forest corridor.

experiences.name: Trek Saptasajya's seven hills
experiences.description: Follow forest trails past waterfalls to the Raghunath Temple, especially lively during Ramanavami.

experiences.name: Tour the royal Rajbati
experiences.description: Walk the grounds of Odisha's only fort-cum-palace and learn about the royal family that once ruled Dhenkanal.

attractions.description: A 12th–13th century Shiva shrine atop Mount Kapilash, reached via 1,352 stone steps or a motorable hill road, prized for its Kalinga-style architecture and views.
attractions.name: Kapilash Temple

attractions.description: A forest sanctuary and vital elephant corridor linking Dhenkanal to Athagarh and Cuttack, with an elephant rescue centre caring for injured and orphaned elephants.
attractions.name: Kapilash Wildlife Sanctuary

attractions.description: Odisha's only fort-cum-palace, built by the local royal family in the late 19th century on the site of a fort that withstood Maratha sieges.
attractions.name: Dhenkanal Palace (Rajbati)

attractions.description: A cluster of seven forested hills about 11 km from town, with the hilltop Raghunath Temple, seasonal waterfalls, and a small wildlife sanctuary.
attractions.name: Saptasajya

attractions.description: Sarana Srikhetra, Dhenkanal — a beautiful Jagannath temple known for its peaceful spiritual atmosphere, where devotees can experience the essence of Jagannath culture and seek Mahaprabhu’s blessings.
attractions.name: Sarana Srikhetra Temple
Maa Ramachandi Temple Nadhara
attractions.description: Maa Ramachandi Temple, Dhenkanal — a peaceful spiritual destination where devotees visit to seek Maa Ramachandi’s blessings while experiencing the temple’s serene and devotional atmosphere.

attractions.name: Sapua Dam
attractions.description: Sapua Dam, Dhenkanal — a peaceful nature getaway surrounded by lush green hills and scenic water views, perfect for picnics, photography, and a relaxing day away from the city.

name: Dubai
tagline: A futuristic desert metropolis where record-breaking skyscrapers meet golden dunes and centuries-old souks.
description: Dubai is a dazzling desert metropolis in the UAE, home to the world's tallest building the Burj Khalifa, man-made islands, luxury souks, and thrilling desert safaris.

local_food.name: Al Machboos
local_food.description: A spiced rice dish with meat or fish, the Emirati answer to biryani, slow-cooked with dried lime and warm spices.

local_food.name: Shawarma
local_food.description: Spit-roasted meat wrapped in flatbread with garlic sauce and pickles — a Dubai street-food staple available everywhere.

local_food.name: Luqaimat
local_food.description: Small, deep-fried dumplings drizzled with date syrup, a popular Emirati dessert especially during Ramadan.

local_food.name: Karak Chai
local_food.description: Strong, spiced milk tea sold at street-side cafeterias across the city, best enjoyed with a fresh samosa.

experiences.name: Desert safari
experiences.description: Dune-bash by 4x4 into the Arabian desert for camel rides, sandboarding, and a Bedouin-style dinner with live entertainment under the stars.

experiences.name: Ride to the top of Burj Khalifa
experiences.description: Book sunset entry to the observation decks for the city skyline turning gold, then lit up at night.

experiences.name: Cruise the Marina or Creek
experiences.description: Take a modern yacht cruise through Dubai Marina or a traditional dhow dinner cruise along Dubai Creek.

experiences.name: Shop the Gold and Spice Souks
experiences.description: Wander Deira's centuries-old souks for gold jewellery, spices, and textiles, then compare with the ultra-modern Dubai Mall.

attractions.name: Burj Khalifa
attractions.description: The world's tallest building at 828m, with observation decks on the 124th, 125th and 148th floors offering panoramic desert-and-skyline views.

attractions.name: Palm Jumeirah
attractions.description: A man-made palm-shaped island lined with luxury resorts, beach clubs, and The View at The Palm observation deck.

attractions.name: Dubai Mall & Dubai Fountain
attractions.description: One of the world's largest malls, anchored by an aquarium and ice rink, with the choreographed Dubai Fountain show right outside.

attractions.name: Dubai Creek & Al Fahidi Historic District
attractions.description: The old trading heart of the city — wind-tower houses, textile and spice souks, and abra boat crossings across the Creek.

name: Kanyakumari
tagline: India's southernmost point, where three seas meet under one sunrise and one sunset.
description: Kanyakumari sits at India's southernmost tip, where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean meet — famous for its sunrise-sunset views and the Vivekananda Rock Memorial.

local_food.name: Kerala-Tamil Thali
local_food.description: A regional fusion thali reflecting the nearby Kerala and Tamil Nadu borders.

local_food.name: Fresh Seafood
local_food.description: Locally caught fish and prawns, grilled or curried, from the surrounding seas.

local_food.name: Filter Coffee
local_food.description: Strong South Indian coffee, a staple at every local eatery.

local_food.name: Banana Chips
local_food.description: Crisp fried banana slices, a popular South Indian snack.

experiences.name: Watch sunrise and sunset
experiences.description: See both from the same beach, a rarity thanks to Kanyakumari's southern-tip geography.

experiences.name: Ferry to Vivekananda Rock
experiences.description: Take the short ferry ride out to the memorial and Thiruvalluvar statue.

experiences.name: Browse the seashell market
experiences.description: Shop for shell crafts and souvenirs along the beachfront market street.

experiences.name: Visit Padmanabhapuram Palace
experiences.description: Tour the intricately carved wooden halls of this centuries-old royal palace.

attractions.name: Vivekananda Rock Memorial
attractions.description: A memorial on a rock islet offshore, reachable by ferry, marking where Swami Vivekananda meditated.

attractions.name: Thiruvalluvar Statue
attractions.description: A 133-foot statue of the Tamil poet-saint standing beside the Vivekananda Rock.

attractions.name: Kanyakumari Beach
attractions.description: The confluence point of three seas, famous for its shared sunrise-sunset viewing spot.

attractions.name: Padmanabhapuram Palace
attractions.description: A well-preserved 16th-century wooden palace, about 30 minutes from town.

name: Kashmir
tagline: Houseboats on Dal Lake, alpine meadows, and snow-lined valleys — India's Himalayan crown.
description: Kashmir, nestled in the Himalayas, is famed for the houseboats of Dal Lake, the alpine meadows of Gulmarg, and the snow-capped valleys of Pahalgam and Sonmarg.

local_food.name: Rogan Josh
local_food.description: A rich, aromatic Kashmiri lamb curry cooked in a blend of Kashmiri red chilli and spices.

local_food.name: Wazwan
local_food.description: A traditional multi-course Kashmiri feast served at weddings and special occasions.

local_food.name: Kahwa
local_food.description: A fragrant green tea infused with saffron, cardamom and almonds.

local_food.name: Kashmiri Pulao
local_food.description: A mildly sweet, fragrant rice dish studded with dried fruits and nuts.

experiences.name: Shikara ride at sunset
experiences.description: Glide across Dal Lake in a traditional shikara as the sun sets over the mountains.

experiences.name: Gulmarg gondola ride
experiences.description: Ride the two-stage cable car up to Apharwat Peak for snow-capped panoramas.

experiences.name: Horseback through Pahalgam
experiences.description: Trek by pony through Pahalgam's meadows and pine forests.

experiences.name: Walk the Mughal Gardens
experiences.description: Stroll the terraced fountains and flowerbeds of Shalimar and Nishat Bagh.

attractions.name: Dal Lake & Houseboats
attractions.description: Srinagar's iconic lake, lined with ornately carved houseboats and floating gardens.

attractions.name: Gulmarg Gondola
attractions.description: One of the world's highest cable cars, rising to Apharwat Peak above the meadows.

attractions.name: Pahalgam Valley
attractions.description: A pine-forested valley along the Lidder River, gateway to the Amarnath Yatra.

attractions.name: Mughal Gardens
attractions.description: Terraced Mughal-era gardens — Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh — overlooking Dal Lake.

name: Kerala
tagline: God's Own Country — backwaters, beaches, hills and living traditions
best_time_to_visit: November to February for cooler, drier weather; September to May is generally pleasant. June to August brings the southwest monsoon.
description: Kerala is a lush tropical state on India’s Malabar Coast, where palm-fringed backwaters, Arabian Sea beaches, wildlife-rich forests and the tea-covered Western Ghats sit within easy reach of one another. Cruise Alappuzha by houseboat, explore Kochi’s layered heritage, unwind in Munnar, discover regional cuisine and experience vibrant festivals, Ayurveda and performing arts.
budget_range: ₹30,000–₹75,000 per person for 7 days, excluding travel to Kerala
nearest_airport: Cochin International Airport (Kochi); Thiruvananthapuram and Calicut airports also serve the state

local_food.name: Kerala sadya
local_food.description: A festive vegetarian feast served on a banana leaf, usually with rice, curries, pickles, papadam and payasam.

local_food.name: Appam with stew and Malabar biryani
local_food.description: Try lace-edged appam with fragrant stew, plus the layered, spice-rich biryani traditions of northern Kerala.

experiences.name: Cruise the backwaters
experiences.description: Spend a day—or an overnight stay—aboard a responsibly operated Kerala houseboat.

experiences.name: Experience Ayurveda
experiences.description: Choose a qualified, certified centre for traditional wellness treatments and rejuvenation programmes.

experiences.name: Watch Kathakali and Kalaripayattu
experiences.description: See Kerala’s vivid classical dance-drama and dynamic martial-art traditions in a cultural performance.

experiences.name: Explore beaches and coastal life
experiences.description: Relax at Kovalam or Varkala, enjoy Arabian Sea sunsets and sample fresh coastal flavours.

attractions.name: Alappuzha Backwaters
attractions.description: Glide through palm-lined canals and lagoons on a traditional houseboat, with village life unfolding along the banks.

attractions.name: Munnar
attractions.description: Explore rolling tea estates, misty viewpoints and cool highland landscapes in the Western Ghats.

attractions.name: Fort Kochi
attractions.description: Walk through a historic waterfront quarter shaped by Indian, Arab, Chinese and European influences, with galleries and Chinese fishing nets.

attractions.name: Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: Discover forested hills and Periyar Lake near Thekkady, known for wildlife viewing, nature walks and boating.

name: Pattaya
tagline: Bangkok's easy beach escape — bold nightlife by night, island boat trips by day.
description: Pattaya is a lively Thai beach resort city known for its nightlife, water sports, floating markets, and easy day trips to nearby islands like Koh Larn.
nearest_airport: U-Tapao Rayong-Pattaya International Airport (about 35 km) or Bangkok Suvarnabhumi (about 110 km)

local_food.name: Tom Yum Goong
local_food.description: Hot-and-sour shrimp soup, a Thai classic found at every seaside restaurant.

local_food.name: Pad Thai
local_food.description: Stir-fried noodles with tofu, egg, shrimp and peanuts.

local_food.name: Grilled seafood
local_food.description: Fresh catch grilled beachside along Jomtien Beach's evening stalls.

local_food.name: Mango Sticky Rice
local_food.description: Sweet coconut sticky rice served with ripe mango, Thailand's favourite dessert.

experiences.name: Koh Larn day trip
experiences.description: Speedboat out to Koh Larn for a calmer beach day and snorkelling.

experiences.name: Water sports
experiences.description: Try parasailing, jet-skiing or banana boating along Jomtien and Pattaya beaches.

experiences.name: Walking Street nightlife
experiences.description: Experience Pattaya's famous strip of bars, clubs and street performances.

experiences.name: Floating market visit
experiences.description: Browse boats selling food and crafts at one of Pattaya's floating markets.

attractions.name: Pattaya Beach & Walking Street
attractions.description: The city's main beachfront by day, transforming into a neon nightlife strip after dark.

attractions.name: Koh Larn (Coral Island)
attractions.description: A quieter island a short speedboat ride away, known for clear water and water sports.

attractions.name: Sanctuary of Truth
attractions.description: An all-wood temple-like structure carved entirely in traditional Thai and Khmer style.

attractions.name: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden
attractions.description: A sprawling botanical garden with cultural shows and landscaped topiary.

name: Phuket
tagline: Thailand's biggest island, where jungle-backed beaches meet the buzz of Patong by night.
description: Phuket is Thailand's largest island, famous for its palm-fringed beaches, vibrant Patong nightlife, limestone cliffs, and easy boat access to the Phi Phi Islands.
nearest_airport: Phuket International Airport — about 30 km from Patong

local_food.name: Pad Thai
local_food.description: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, tofu/shrimp, peanuts and lime — Thailand's signature street dish.

local_food.name: Tom Yum Goong
local_food.description: A hot-and-sour shrimp soup with lemongrass, galangal and chilli.

local_food.name: Moo Hong
local_food.description: A Phuket-style braised pork belly dish, sweet and dark from slow-cooked soy and palm sugar.

local_food.name: Roti
local_food.description: A crisp fried pancake street snack, served sweet with banana and condensed milk or savoury.

experiences.name: Island-hop to Phi Phi
experiences.description: Take a speedboat day trip to Phi Phi Don and Phi Phi Leh for snorkelling and Maya Bay.

experiences.name: Patong nightlife
experiences.description: Spend an evening on Bangla Road's bars, night markets and cabaret shows.

experiences.name: Explore Old Town
experiences.description: Walk the Sino-Portuguese shophouse streets and try local coffee and Thai desserts.

experiences.name: Sunset at a viewpoint
experiences.description: Catch sunset from Karon or Promthep Cape viewpoint over the Andaman Sea.

attractions.name: Patong Beach
attractions.description: Phuket's liveliest beach strip, backed by Bangla Road's bars, clubs and night markets.

attractions.name: Big Buddha Phuket
attractions.description: A 45m marble-clad Buddha statue on Nakkerd Hill with panoramic island views.

attractions.name: Old Phuket Town
attractions.description: Sino-Portuguese shophouses, street art and heritage cafes in the island's historic quarter.

attractions.name: Phi Phi Islands
attractions.description: A dramatic limestone-cliff island group reachable by day-trip speedboat, including Maya Bay.

name: Puri
tagline: Where the Bay of Bengal meets centuries of faith, art and coastal life.
best_time_to_visit: October to February; June or July for Rath Yatra
description:
Puri is Odisha's celebrated coastal pilgrimage city and one of India's four sacred Char Dham destinations. 
Beyond Sri Jagannath Temple, travellers discover golden beaches, colourful markets, traditional crafts, Odia cuisine and a living calendar of festivals led by the famous Rath Yatra, coastal side of Chilika and historical Konark Sun temple.
nearest_airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar — about 60 km

local_food.name: Mahaprasad
local_food.description: The sacred temple offering prepared in traditional earthen pots and shared as part of Puri's devotional culture.

local_food.name: Chhena Poda
local_food.description: A caramelised baked cottage-cheese dessert and one of Odisha's best-known sweets.

local_food.name: Dalma
local_food.description: A comforting Odia preparation of lentils and vegetables, gently seasoned and widely available.

local_food.name: Machha Besara
local_food.description: Fish cooked in a distinctive mustard-based gravy for a taste of coastal Odia cuisine.

local_food.name: Chingudi Tarkari
local_food.description: Prawn curry that reflects Puri's access to fresh seafood from the Bay of Bengal.

experiences.name: Watch sunrise on Puri Beach
experiences.description: Start before the crowds and see the fishing coast and temple city wake beside the Bay of Bengal.

experiences.name: Walk the old city and markets
experiences.description: Explore Grand Road, devotional neighbourhoods, handicrafts and the everyday rhythm around the temple.

experiences.name: Discover Odishan craft
experiences.description: Visit Raghurajpur and nearby Pipili to understand Pattachitra and colourful appliqué traditions.

experiences.name: Take a heritage day trip
experiences.description: Combine the Konark Sun Temple and the Puri–Konark Marine Drive for architecture and coastal scenery.

attractions.name: Sri Jagannath Temple
attractions.description: The spiritual heart of Puri and a major Char Dham pilgrimage site, renowned for its rituals, architecture and Rath Yatra.

attractions.name: Puri Beach
attractions.description: A broad golden shoreline for sunrise walks, sea views, sand art and the lively seafront atmosphere.

attractions.name: Gundicha Temple
attractions.description: An important Rath Yatra landmark traditionally known as Lord Jagannath's destination during the festival.

attractions.name: Raghurajpur Heritage Crafts Village
attractions.description: Meet artisan families and discover Pattachitra painting, palm-leaf engraving and traditional performance.

attractions.name: Narendra Sarovar
attractions.description: A historic sacred tank closely associated with the annual Chandan Yatra celebrations.

attractions.name: Balighai Beach
attractions.description: A quieter coastal escape north of Puri, suited to travellers looking beyond the main beachfront.
